title: Leukocyte diversity did not establish added transported CRP prediction beyond routine blood-count summaries
abstract: Five-part leukocyte Shannon entropy was tested as a compact representation of information discarded by WBC count and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). In a locked source-to-target analysis of newly acquired NHANES releases, 3,906 adults from 2001–2002 trained models evaluated in 3,787 separately sampled adults from 2003–2004. Adding entropy reduced target mean squared error of natural-log CRP from 1.128537 to 1.124930: difference -0.003607, rescaled PSU-bootstrap 95% interval [-0.008948, 0.001803]. This did **not** satisfy the registered criterion for a reliable gain. Source-and-target refitting gave interval [-0.014394, 0.047915]. Entropy also failed to establish gain beyond the full differential. This is a negative incremental-prediction result, not evidence that leukocyte composition is biologically uninformative or that the true effect is zero.
